chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the khumisa (a type of garment for ihram) whose warp is silk and its weft is from wool. He said, 'There is no harm in being prohibited (in ihram) in it; only the pure silk is disliked (for ihram).'

key_terms.الْخَمِيصَة: A specific type of garment (often a shirt or tunic) worn by men during ihram.
key_terms.غَزْل: Wool or spun fiber used as weft.
key_terms.لَحْمَة: The weft (horizontal threads) of a woven fabric.
key_terms.يُحْرَمَ: To be in the state of ihram (ritual consecration).

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear a silk-and-wool mixed garment during Hajm ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between pure silk (*khamis al-khalis*) and mixed silk garments during the sacred state of *ihram*, establishing that the prohibition applies specifically to pure silk while mixed fabrics remain permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the restriction on silk is rooted in its exclusivity as a luxury for men, rather than a general prohibition on all silk blends, thereby facilitating practical compliance for pilgrims.
